key_insight: Y6 film excitons are hybrid Frenkel-charge-transfer states with 20–40% charge-transfer character, and their quenching is governed by delocalization-assisted short-range transport rather than purely diffusive hopping.
engineering_relevance: This provides a quantitative design rule for optimizing single-component organic solar cells by tuning interface coupling, exciton delocalization, and ultrafast charge extraction.
method: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy on Y6 films near hole-transport interfaces.
Analytical hybrid Frenkel-charge-transfer model to fit quenching dynamics and extract microscopic parameters.
Direct estimation of electronic coupling, charge-transfer admixture, and system-bath interaction strengths.
evidence_signal: Experimental transient absorption data show ~1 ps exciton quenching within ~4 nm of the interface, supporting a short-range injection mechanism.
watch_item: The extracted transport picture is system- and interface-dependent, so the model should be validated before generalizing to other acceptors or device stacks.
paper_title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells
